A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SHIELD with the same authors, core method and shared experiments. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on CHAIR, POPE, MME and LLaVA-Bench, together with module ablations, sensitivity studies and inference measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical evaluations and adds benchmark results, newer-model evaluations, expanded comparisons and controlled analyses.

M1.justification: SHIELD retains caption-guided token reweighting, averaged noise-token subtraction, learned adversarial perturbations, contrastive decoding and plausibility filtering. Equations 1–16 are unchanged. FGSM and PGD are tested as ablation alternatives; they do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds AMBER's generative and discriminative hallucination evaluation and MMHal-Bench's eight open-ended categories, including environment and holistic descriptions. It also adds noise-token replacement and corrupted-caption test conditions. The earlier benchmark coverage remains.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's vanilla, VCD and OPERA comparisons, v2 Table 16 evaluates DoLa, ICD, TAME, SID, LLaVA-RLHF, CCA-LLaVA, Less is More and MCA-LLaVA on CHAIR. This substantially expands comparison methods, including training-based approaches. HALC, MARINE and VTI are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Added protocols include AMBER metrics, GPT-4 judging for MMHal-Bench, and Qwen2-VL/2.5-VL 7B and Qwen3-VL 8B configurations. Efficiency evaluation changes from POPE latency to CHAIR latency and peak memory. New controls specify ten questions per object and attack-step/strategy sweeps. Existing experiments retain their stated settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds attack-step sensitivity testing, noise-image versus noise-token controls for encoder bias, robustness testing with hallucinated naive captions, FGSM/PGD comparisons, and module-level computational-cost analysis. These test substantive questions beyond v1's analyses. Existing module and hyperparameter ablations and the two original case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated benchmark-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new ten-question-per-category control specifies evaluation sample size. Averaging K noise inputs was already part of SHIELD and is not newly introduced uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original matched performance tables retain their values, but v2 adds substantial results: AMBER scores of 88.0 for SHIELD versus 86.5 for OPERA, MMHal overall scores of 2.65 versus vanilla's 2.21, and newer-model, baseline and controlled-analysis results. V1's POPE timing entries are removed and CHAIR profiling is added, preventing direct speed comparisons. New Table 16 gives OPERA CS as 44.8, inconsistent with 44.6 in retained Table 1.

T1.justification: The inference equations and CHAIR definitions are unchanged. The added appendix explanations are empirical or conceptual; they introduce no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same encoder-focused novelty claim, three-part training-free framework, hallucination-reduction claim and broader perception benefits. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations attributing overhead to caption generation and adversarial optimization, arguing that plausible caption hallucinations usually have weak visual grounding, and motivating learned perturbations over fixed-step attacks. Existing qualifications concerning Q-Former and reduced reliance on prior knowledge remain. These are targeted extensions of the original interpretation.

D1.justification: The abstract supplies a code-repository link where v1 only promised release. V2 also documents attack-step settings and module-specific resource requirements, while retaining the main hyperparameters and GPU specification. Disclosure remains imperfect: the reproducibility statement still promises future release, and the MMHal evaluator is identified only as the latest GPT-4.

R1.justification: Related work adds descriptions of HALC, MARINE and VTI, with further references supporting the expanded comparisons, benchmarks and adversarial-attack analysis. These broaden the literature context, but the training-required/training-free organization and encoder-focused novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and heading revisions, updates affiliations, and adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements. Appendices gain several subsections, while the main narrative remains largely unchanged. The original case-study section moves from Appendix D to E rather than becoming a new study.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an ICLR layout with narrower text, revised headings and recurring headers, substantially reflowing figures and tables. It adds benchmark, comparison, efficiency and control tables plus a new caption-example figure. The original case-study figure is reformatted and relabeled from CCD to SHIELD; the POPE timing table is removed.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical validation. Table 16 addresses v1's narrow baseline comparison, Appendix D adds controls for encoder attribution and misleading captions, and new benchmarks and models test broader applicability. Module-level profiling also clarifies computational tradeoffs. These additions materially improve support for the central claims despite remaining weaknesses, including the OPERA discrepancy, unspecified MMHal evaluator version and absent uncertainty estimates.
